snippet.text: - The coordinator may do two things in the maintainer's place, and nothing else, and neither on a pull request it wrote: dismiss an equivalent mutant, and dismiss a refuted injection flag on a line of Melian's own prompt text that the change only moved. Every policy notice is the maintainer's to read, the override status of the outage procedure is his to post, and a finding that restates a ruling is his to dismiss. For each, the coordinator sends him one message that quotes the change or the finding, and records his answer on the pull request. [The decision](docs/decisions/2026-11-28-what-the-coordinator-may-do-for-the-maintainer.md) says why.

explanation.whatToDo: Split the sentence at its seams. For example: "The coordinator may do two things in the maintainer's place, and nothing else. It may dismiss an equivalent mutant. It may dismiss a refuted injection flag on a line of Melian's own prompt text that the change only moved. It does neither on a pull request it wrote."
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md's Writing rules say: "If a sentence runs past about 25 words, find the seam." They also say "One thought per sentence, one idea per paragraph." These rules cover docs, and this line is the rule that builders will check the coordinator against. At 44 words, the sentence is well past the limit.

properties.failureScenario: A builder wants to know whether the coordinator may dismiss a finding on the builder's pull request. To find out, it has to work through one 44-word sentence. In that sentence the exclusion "neither on a pull request it wrote" sits between "nothing else" and the colon that introduces the two permitted acts. A reader can easily take the exclusion as part of the list, or miss it altogether. AGENTS.md's rule to split any sentence past about 25 words exists to stop exactly that.
